text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Some 40 parties and coalitions are going to contest in Bulgaria's general election due on April 19, the Central Electoral Commission said. Election campaign starts today.
-- Food prices rose 418 percent from the beginning of the year, the director of trade unions' Institute for Social Researches Roumyana Kraleva said. @

-- Bulgaria should now be able to buy 100,000 tonnes of European Union intervention bread wheat to ensure supplies until the next crop, EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler told the EU farm ministers in Brussels.
-- Some 75 percent of Bulgarians approve of the economic stabilisation measures by the country's caretaker cabinet, which took office last month, a survey by Market Test polling agency showed. @

-- Germany was ready to invest in Bulgaria some two billion marks if economic reforms in the Balkan country got enough support in the new parliament after April 19 general election, German officials said diring a visit to Germany by the chairman of the Bulgarian-German Forum Valentin Vassilev.
-- The Sofia City Court will rule on an insolvency case against state-owned Mineralbank filed by the Bulgarian National Bank by end-March, said a Mineralbank sequestrator.

-- Bulgaria's central bank is to adjust its main interest rate to market conditions each week instead of each month under recommendations by the International Monetary Fund included in a financial accord reached on Monday.

-- Changes could be expected in the management bodies of Bulgaria's state-owned Biochim Bank, said an official from the Bank Consolidation Company, which manages state equity in local commercial banks.
-- Bulgaria's railway passenger fares rise by 150 percent today. @

-- Bulgaria's Supreme Administrative Court last week overturned a decision by the previous Socialist government to refuse to register Fikri Sali's High Moslem Coincil, the alternative Chief Mufti Sali said and appealed to the new cabinet to register his council. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
